Class SlotSpec

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.slot.SlotSpec
public final class SlotSpec extends Object
A side-neutral description of one group of registered slots that a ParityGroup adds to every container the player opens. It is the recipe half of container parity.

Why a recipe and not a built slot

A real CreatedSlot belongs to one menu. The player's own InventoryMenu, every chest or furnace they open, and the creative item picker each carry their own slot instance for the same logical slot. To put a slot on all of them from one registration, the group can't hold a slot. It holds the instructions to build one, applied to each menu and bound to that menu's player. That is this class: plain data plus a Player -> Storage factory, evaluated the same way on the logical server and the client so the appended slots are byte-identical (see CreatedSlotProjection on sync safety).

It holds the same settings as the per-call parameters on CreatedSlots.Builder (storage, label, the client reveal predicate), but as reusable data instead of calls against one menu. ParityGroup.register(String, SlotSpec) turns a SlotSpec into the real slots (every menu, both sides). The mod's own panel shows them (SlotFlowElement.of(group), client).

Behavior methods set it once for the whole group

Gating, shift-click, collect, drag-fill, binding and mending live in the window engine, the same for a vanilla slot and a created slot. The methods here (gate, accepts(Predicate), binding, mending, shiftClickOut, shiftClickIn, collect, dragFill) don't add a second place to store behavior. They record what the consumer asked for, and ParityGroup.register(String, SlotSpec) sets it in the engine once, on the group's own key (GroupKey.of(group.id())), one level above any single slot. Behavior is declared next to the slot group, with no separate step to forget and no per-slot loop. To give one slot something else, set it on that slot's address, Window.slot(scope, Address.createdSlot(group.id(), i)); the slot's own value wins because it is more specific.

Storage is a factory, not bound storage

CreatedSlots.Builder.storage takes a Storage already bound to a player, because it runs inside a mixin where the player is in scope. A recipe is registered once at init with no player in scope and applied to many players' menus, so it takes a Function<Player, Storage>, almost always player -> SOME_ATTACHMENT.bind(player). The factory must be deterministic and give the same storage size for a given player on both sides, or the appended slots desync.

A mutable builder, used once by ParityGroup.register(String, SlotSpec).

  • Method Details

    • at

      public static SlotSpec at(String groupId, SlotGroupCategory category)
      Starts a slot-group spec. Position is not declared: the group's slots flow and wrap to the owning panel's width through SlotFlowElement, so a spec only says what a group is (storage, count, reveal, behavior), never where it sits.

      The category is required, and it is the group's identity. It is how other mods find these slots (SlotGroupCategories.of(menu) lists created groups next to vanilla ones) and tell what they are. A pocket group declared SlotGroupCategory.PLAYER_INVENTORY counts as player inventory to a search; an elytra slot under the mod's own category does not. There is no default on purpose: a group that forgot to say what it is would silently look like plain storage to every consumer, which is the dangerous outcome. Once another mod depends on a category name it is a public contract, and renaming it is a breaking change.

      Parameters:
      groupId - slot-group id, unique within its owner (ParityGroup.register(String, SlotSpec))
      category - what the group is: a vanilla category, or one the mod declares (new SlotGroupCategory("mymod", "pockets"))

    • storage

      public SlotSpec storage(Function<net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player, Storage> storageFactory)
      Where items live, as a per-player factory. Required. To persist content, bind from a StorageAttachment: .storage(player -> POCKETS.bind(player)).

    • count

      public SlotSpec count(int count)
      Number of slots in this group (default 1). The storage factory must give storage of exactly this size for every player, or the appended slots desync between the sides.

    • activeCount

      public SlotSpec activeCount(int startCount)
      Opts the group in to a server-set active count, starting at startCount: slot i is live while i < count, and every slot from the count on is inert on both sides (empty to the client, refusing clicks), so the server opens and closes the group and sizes it per player (ParityGroup.setActiveCount(ServerPlayer, int)). Declare the largest size you need with count; only the count moves. A group without this is always its full count, with no sync traffic.
      Parameters:
      startCount - the count a player starts at, on login and after death, from 0 to count

    • revealWhen

      public SlotSpec revealWhen(BooleanSupplier clientReveal)
      Client-side reveal predicate. The group is visible and usable on the client only while this returns true; the server keeps it syncing either way (see CreatedSlots.Builder.revealWhen). Must be client-safe. If unset, the group is always visible.

    • label

      public SlotSpec label(String label)
      Display name for the group's slots, applied like CreatedSlots.Builder.label(String): each slot is named "{label} {n}" (from 1) in a multi-slot group, or just "{label}" for a single slot. If unset, the slots use the capitalized group id. Names are client-side only; the build step applies them only on the client.

    • tooltip

      public SlotSpec tooltip(net.minecraft.network.chat.Component text)
      Adds a hover tooltip to every slot in this group. The library applies it to each SlotElement it builds, so the consumer never touches those. Shows only over an empty slot; a slot holding an item shows vanilla's item tooltip instead. Chainable.

    • tooltip

      public SlotSpec tooltip(@Nullable Supplier<net.minecraft.network.chat.Component> supplier)

    • emptyIcon

      public SlotSpec emptyIcon(net.minecraft.resources.Identifier sprite)
      The outline drawn on each empty slot of this group, as vanilla draws the armor and offhand outlines: a GUI sprite id, returned from the slot's getNoItemIcon, so vanilla draws it in its own slot pass, under any item and in creative too. Identifier.withDefaultNamespace("container/slot/shield") names a vanilla sprite; Identifier.fromNamespaceAndPath("mymod", "container/slot/elytra") is a mod's own, at assets/mymod/textures/gui/sprites/container/slot/elytra.png. Since 1.1.0.

    • gate

      public SlotSpec gate(SlotGate gate)
      Sets a SlotGate: what every slot in this group accepts, releases and caps at, set once for the group. Unset, it is SlotGate.OPEN, plain vanilla.

    • accepts

      public SlotSpec accepts(Predicate<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack> accept)
      A placement-only filter, shorthand for gate. Builds a SlotGate that accepts a stack only if accept passes; pickup stays open and the stack cap stays vanilla. For a pickup rule or stack cap, pass a full SlotGate to gate.

    • shiftClickIn

      public SlotSpec shiftClickIn(boolean enabled)
      Whether a shift-click elsewhere may put items in this group, set for the group (BehaviorKeys.SHIFT_CLICK_IN). Default on.

      shiftClickIn(true), said explicitly, also makes the group a shift-click target in the player's inventory (since 1.1.0). Vanilla's own routing there never reaches a created slot, so SlotKit tries these groups first: partial stacks, then empty slots, each slot judged by the group's gate. What doesn't fit goes where vanilla sends it. .accepts(isElytra).shiftClickIn(true) is a whole elytra slot. Out of a created slot, shift-click goes to the main inventory, then the hotbar, as vanilla does for any slot past the offhand.

    • collect

      public SlotSpec collect(boolean enabled)
      Whether vanilla's double-click collect may pull items out of this group. Shorthand for set(BehaviorKeys.COLLECT, ...). Default on, as in vanilla. A storage group the bulk shortcuts must not touch declares .shiftClickOut(false).shiftClickIn(false).collect(false).dragFill(false).

    • dragFill

      public SlotSpec dragFill(boolean enabled)
      Whether vanilla's drag-fill (spreading a carried stack across dragged-over slots) may place into this group. Shorthand for set(BehaviorKeys.DRAG_FILL, ...). Default on, as in vanilla.
